surface_mechanism_description: Surface reactions stop and saturate when the reactive sites of the surface are completely depleted. The first step is the injection of one-pulsed deionized (DI) H2O into a reactor to make hydroxyl (OH)-terminated surface on sapphire or to react with the dangling ethyl groups (C2H5) forming zinc-oxygen (Zn–O) bridges on Zn surface with hydroxyl surface groups. The third step is the injection of three-pulsed O3 into reactors to facilitate the reduction of native defects. The fifth step is the injection of one-pulsed DEZn into reactors to produce one atomic layer of zinc (Zn) upon the oxygen layer.
